headline: Unannounced Nvidia RTX 50 Super GPUs appear in Seasonic PSU calculator with 10-17% higher TGP
summary: Seasonic's PSU wattage calculator lists unreleased RTX 50 Super models, hinting at significant TGP increases of 10-17% over their non-Super counterparts, though Nvidia has not confirmed these specifications.
details: Unannounced Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 Super, RTX 5070 Ti Super, and RTX 5070 Super GPUs have appeared in Seasonic's PSU wattage calculator. These listings suggest board power increases of 10-17% over existing RTX 50-series models. This information is unconfirmed by Nvidia.

The purported RTX 5080 Super is listed with a 415W board power, a 15% increase from the existing RTX 5080's 360W. This could be due to higher power limits, more aggressive clock speeds, or potentially 8GB more GDDR7 memory.

The RTX 5070 Ti Super shows a 350W rating, 17% higher than the RTX 5070 Ti. The RTX 5070 Super sees a 10% TGP bump from 250W to 275W. These cards might also see performance boosts from enabling more Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs).

While TGP increases are noted, real-world performance benefits may be smaller than the percentages suggest. Our testing indicates that the largest gains from higher power limits are often concentrated in computationally intensive ray-traced and path-traced games.

Nvidia is not expected to release these products soon, currently focusing on software improvements like DLSS 4.5 and Multi-Frame Generation for existing Blackwell silicon. These technologies enhance frame rates and image quality.

However, with rising monitor refresh rates and future HDMI 2.2 connectors, a hardware update boosting baseline performance and supporting new standards seems practical. An announcement at CES 2027 or Computex 2027 could be possible, but remains speculative.

headline: OpenAI's Chief Futurist Joshua Achiam is leaving after nearly nine years
summary: Joshua Achiam, a key figure in AI safety and policy, is departing OpenAI this month. His exit follows several other safety-focused leaders as the company prepares for a potential IPO.
details: OpenAI's chief futurist, Joshua Achiam, is leaving the company later this month after nearly nine years. Achiam stated his departure was not for any specific reason, but he believes it's possible to work on the AI mission from outside a frontier lab.

Achiam's role sat at the intersection of OpenAI’s AI safety and policy teams, studying potential harms and benefits of AI. He worked with senior leaders to advocate for government regulations aligned with OpenAI's mission of ensuring AGI benefits all humanity.

OpenAI has undergone numerous reorganizations since ChatGPT's 2022 launch, rapidly growing from a research lab. In 2024, Achiam led a "mission alignment team" which was later disbanded in February, leading to his chief futurist role.

Achiam is the latest safety-focused leader to depart OpenAI. Jan Leike, co-lead of the Superalignment team, left for Anthropic in 2024. Miles Brundage and Steven Adler also left to found nonprofits advocating for strong AI safety standards.

Achiam joined OpenAI as an intern in 2017 and became a research scientist focused on AI safety. He was known internally as a strong defender of OpenAI’s safety mission, despite occasional criticisms of the broader AI safety community.

A notable incident involved Achiam interrupting Elon Musk's parting speech in 2018, questioning Tesla's AGI plans regarding safety. Musk reportedly called him a "jackass," a moment later commemorated by colleagues with a golden donkey statue.
